first.text:
Here's what adopting this change would record, and everything it raises. Nothing is written yet.

**What changes**

1. **Pull-up target.** Negatives and band pull-ups now add to the strict pull-up's weekly figure, one hard set each, and the target moves from 1 to **10 hard sets a week**. My reasoning: the week as written plans 3 negatives, 7 band sets and the strict single, about 11 hard sets when it's all done. Ten sits just under that, so a full week clears it with one set to spare, a cut set or a skipped Wednesday shows up as a miss, and it matches the 10 per muscle everywhere else. Eight (the default for a lift) would be cleared even on a soft week and tell us nothing; twelve would be missed any time a set drops. The old note explaining why the target was 1 is gone, and the week no longer raises anything about the pull-up. Your call on the number.

2. **Swings.** The 8×10 finisher leaves Monday's press session. Monday now has two sessions: the lifting, then a separate swing session, every minute on the minute, **12 minutes of 12 reps at 40 lb (18.1 kg), effort 7**, growing by two minutes to a cap of 16 and up to 15 reps as it stays at or under effort 7. I've made it optional, so a skipped Monday evening doesn't count against your week. Monday's lifting estimate drops from **58 to 47 of 75 minutes**; the other sessions are unchanged (Wednesday 39/75, Friday 65/75, Saturday 65/90, Sunday 65/90). Nothing was filled in on your behalf; the block carries on from where it is, same rotation week. Monday the 2nd's logged swings stay exactly as they are and still count in that week's figures.

   On the hard-set question: once swings are logged against their own conditioning session they are read as a conditioning bout, not as lifting sets, so they should stop appearing in the glute and hamstring counts. I can only confirm that against a closed week after the change is in, so I'll check it at the first check-in after you've done one. One thing to know: the weekly plan still asks about a hard conditioning bout within six hours of a lift on the same day. If you do the swings straight after the press, the plan may question the stacking; an evening gap avoids it.

3. **The circuit.** Untouched. Under the new rules a standing session sits outside the stacking check entirely, so the weekly note explaining it shouldn't be needed again. The plan currently in force was built before the upgrade and still carries the old note; the first plan built after this change is where it's confirmed gone.

**What it raises**

- **Deadlift target, new.** With the pull-up note gone, the week now points at the deadlift: its target of 4 hard sets sits below the 5–15 range for a priority lift. It was there all along, hidden behind the pull-up one, because only one of these notes shows at a time. That's a limitation worth reporting; I can write it up if you like. Two ways out: raise the deadlift target to 5, the bottom of the range, or keep 4 with a reason I carry forward (Sunday is the only barbell deadlift day; the PT sometimes adds pulls). I lean to 5 so the target reads the Sunday line honestly. Your call.
- **Strict pull-up test single.** Still carried with its reason: one weekly single is the measure while the max is 1; negatives and band work do the building until the test rep passes about five. Unchanged.
- **A Hevy routine has drifted** from this week's plan: three rep counts on its first exercise and three weights on its second were edited after the push. The next weekly push realigns it. Not caused by this change and not blocked by it; I'm not touching the published routines until your plate work is done, as you asked.

Give me the pull-up number (10 unless you say otherwise) and the deadlift choice (5, or keep 4), say yes, and I'll record it.
